text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin was "highly satisfied" with the results of talks with French leader Jacques Chirac at a country residence outside Moscow on Sunday, Interfax news agency said.

Interfax, quoting Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky, said talks were extended by an hour to allow a broad discussion of issues including relations between NATO and Russia. "This alone tells us that the discussion was a substantial one."
"(Yeltsin said that) on many issues, especially European issues, the positions of Russia and France coincide," Yastrzhembsky added.
He said Chirac listened to Yeltsin's views on NATO with understanding.
Russia objects to NATO plans for eastward expansion, insisting the incorporation of former Moscow allies in the Western grouping would undermine Russian security.
